subject: System Design
title: Live Streaming Architecture
description: A quick, practical guide to Live Streaming Architecture.

hook.text: A million viewers watch a live concert simultaneously. The video must reach everyone within 5 seconds of real time.

buildup.text: Live streams use segmented delivery: the video is chopped into 2-6 second segments and distributed via CDN.

discovery.text: HLS and DASH protocols deliver segments over standard HTTP. No special streaming servers needed — just web servers.

twist.text: True real-time (under 1 second) uses WebRTC, not HLS. But WebRTC doesn't scale to millions without a media server layer.

climax.text: Live streaming trades latency for scalability: 5-30 second delay lets CDNs distribute segments efficiently.

punchline.text: Chop live video into segments, deliver over HTTP via CDN.

quiz.question: Why do live streams have a delay?
options: Segmented delivery via CDN needs time to chop, distribute, and buffer video
